description: I'm building EarthLens, an interactive web app that helps people explore NASA Earth science data, visualize environmental changes, and discover long-term trends. I hope to make Earth science more accessible and engaging through technology and creative visualizations.
summary:
EarthLens is an interactive web platform that helps people investigate environmental change using NASA POWER data. It addresses the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!” challenge by helping users explore where changes occur, how large they are, and whether observed trends are statistically significant.

Users can select locations and time periods, visualize daily or monthly data, and examine regression slopes, R², and p-values. A formula editor supports both text and Scratch-style blocks, allowing users to combine environmental variables and apply time-series operations. Saved formulas can be reused across analyses, compared across different data, and transformed into sound through six synthesized instruments and synchronized audio tracks. Charts and data can also be exported.

By bringing these tools into one accessible workspace, EarthLens lowers the barrier to exploring Earth science and helps users turn complex datasets into observations they can examine, question, and share.
details:
EarthLens helps users explore environmental change through NASA POWER data. Users choose a location, a time range, and either daily or monthly data, then examine time-series charts, regression slopes, R², and p-values. Compare lets users investigate differences between locations or formulas, while export tools make charts and data available for further use.

The formula editor supports both text and Scratch-style blocks. Users can combine variables, apply rolling calculations, and create conditional expressions without writing a separate analysis program. Saved formulas can also be used to create music cards, turning data values into notes played by six synthesized instruments. Multiple cards can play together on separate tracks.

I built EarthLens using React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS for the frontend, and Python, FastAPI, Pandas, and NumPy for the backend. I also used Leaflet for map-based location selection and the Web Audio API to turn data into sound.

EarthLens brings together scientific data analysis, interactive Scratch-style blocks, and music. Users can build formulas visually, examine trends with statistical tools, and hear environmental changes through sound. I considered both analytical depth and ease of use, offering different ways to explore the same data. My goal is to make Earth science more approachable and engaging, encouraging people to ask questions, investigate changes, and share what they find.
